decisions: 1.1: ScopeDimension.OBJECT ('object') added to BUILT_IN; strict-token error message lists OBJECT. DataScope.admits(dimension, value): ALL true, NONE false, RESTRICTED true only for an alternative whose restricted key set is exactly {dimension} and lists the value (null value false). DataScopeTest 6/6 (+2), ScopeGrantTest 7/7 (+1).

1.2: DataScopePolicyValidator: admin.* resources skip the mapping checks (named objects, not rows) and instead must name a catalogued area, use only read/operate/privileged actions, and map roles to ALL or NONE only (a RESTRICTED role entry, e.g. OBJECT, is refused naming the entry and 'granted per subject'). The catalog's areas come through a Supplier from ObjectProvider<AdminOperationCatalog>, read at validation (the admin auto-configuration runs after data's; with the surface off every admin.* policy is refused). The 2-arg constructor is kept (empty areas) so the public type has no break. ScopePolicies gains actionsOf(resource). DataScopePolicyValidatorTest 4/4 (new).

2.1 (deviation from design decision 2): the guard runs as a HandlerInterceptor before argument resolution, so the object is read from the matched URI template (HandlerMapping.URI_TEMPLATE_VARIABLES_ATTRIBUTE) by the @PathVariable's name, not from resolved arguments; the ArchUnit rule (2.2) is what makes that sound. A missing value fails closed.

2.1: identical 404: @AdminObject(notFound = <the area's not-found code>) - AdminObjectNotFoundException renders (NOT_FOUND, code, [object]) exactly as the area's own LocalizedException does; default code ludwig.admin.object-not-found (bundle EN+RU). AdminObjectScope(ScopePolicies, DataScopeProvider) - both null when data scoping is off - with isScoped(area, tier) = a policy entry exists for admin.<area>/tier, admits(principal, area, tier, object), filter(area, tier, names) for listings using the current AdminInvocation. AdminAccessEvaluator gains a 3-arg constructor (2-arg kept) and authorizeObject(...), called by the guard right after authorize(); denials are published like every other (audited). A role absent from the policy gets NONE (PolicyDataScopeProvider), so only grants admit - fail closed.
